title: Handling and Presenting Harmful Text in NLP Research
findings: The paper uses hate speech against Muslims as a key example to illustrate the ethical challenges and potential for harm when handling and presenting sensitive content in NLP research. It argues for the necessity of clear protocols, such as content warnings and careful presentation, to protect readers and reviewers from distress, without presenting specific empirical findings on religious bias in models.

measurement_description: The paper does not introduce a benchmark for measurement. It proposes a framework and checklist (HARMCHECK) for responsibly handling and presenting harmful text in research, which can include religious hate speech.
